clue.text: Master joining a bright star for a dance

definitions.note: the definition names the dance itself, a Brazilian style

parts.note: a master is the person in charge, the boss
a nova is a star that suddenly flares much brighter

explanation.surface: A master of ceremonies pairs up with a shining celebrity for a turn on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazilian dance and music style blending samba with jazz, popular from the late 1950s.

clue.text: Simple when described by writer

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the pen's letters encircle the other word

parts.note: a Bic is a well-known brand of ballpoint pen
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Something plain becomes so once an author has put it into words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described by' is the container signal: BIC, a ballpoint pen, goes round AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic and simple are synonyms for something elementary or plain.

clue.text: Attend rehearsal — it's outcome's predictable

parts.note: to show is to turn up, as in 'he didn't show'
a trial is a test run, a rehearsal

explanation.surface: Going to a dress rehearsal means you already know how the play ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged prosecution, typical of totalitarian regimes, whose guilty verdict is fixed in advance.

clue.text: As lethal? Unlikely — extremely macabre, nevertheless

indicators.note: an unlikely arrangement of these letters is a rearranged one, signalling an anagram
taking a word at its extremes gives its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Doubting that something is deadly, while admitting it is grimly morbid all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlikely' rearranges AS LETHAL into ALLTHESA; 'extremely' takes M and E, the first and last letters of macabre.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning however or in spite of that, just like nevertheless.

clue.text: Affectionate form of address used by former head

parts.note: old can mean former, as in 'my old school'
bean is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A retired headmaster still greets people with a warm, chummy phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAN is old-fashioned British slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated, upper-class British term of endearment between friends, like 'old chap'.

clue.text: As one masked by mobile cranes?

definitions.note: As is the chemical symbol of the element in question

indicators.note: something masked is covered over, so the numeral sits inside the other letters
mobile means moving about, so the letters of cranes are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A question about whether some object could be hidden among moving cranes on a building site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a link word but is the chemical symbol; 'mobile' rearranges CRANES and 'masked by' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is the element whose chemical symbol is As, number 33 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Actress showing dress ring

parts.note: garb is clothing, dress
the letter O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: A film star shows off her outfit and jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a celebrated film star of the silent and early sound era.

clue.text: Set up to sell game

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting something up reads it upwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: flog is British slang meaning to sell

explanation.surface: Something arranged in order to market a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: FLOG is British informal for sell; 'Set up' turns it upward in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a sport played with clubs and a ball on a course.

clue.text: Kingdom in actual miles

parts.note: real means actual, genuine

explanation.surface: A domain measured in true distances.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a monarch's territory, a synonym for kingdom.

clue.text: Clear cut -daughter is paying too much duty

parts.note: overt means open, clear to see
to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: A girl with a clean-cut image is being charged excessive tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtaxed means burdened with excessive tax, so paying more duty than is fair.

clue.text: Dinghy on lake causes one to frown

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed boat

explanation.surface: Sailing a small boat on a lake makes someone grimace.
explanation.definitionFit: To scowl is to frown angrily or with displeasure.

clue.text: Upset in place beset by sickness

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded, so the other letters wrap round

parts.note: disease means sickness
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed to be in a spot surrounded by illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To displease someone is to annoy or offend them, to upset them.

clue.text: Bag offered by girl, using cheapness for appeal

parts.note: to bag is to catch or capture
Penny is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman offers a handbag, pitching its low price as the attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Catchpenny describes something cheap and showy, designed to sell quickly to the unwary.

clue.text: Leave out stuffing from Italy

indicators.note: stuffing sits inside something, so the letters are found within the words

explanation.surface: Skip the stuffing recipe from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffing' points to the letters inside fROM ITaly.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit is to leave out or exclude.

clue.text: Ten men I tip to reform hardened sinner

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A tip of ten men is supposed to straighten out a habitual wrongdoer.
explanation.definitionFit: Impenitent means unrepentant, so an impenitent is a sinner who refuses to repent.

clue.text: Borders in study, a deep red

indicators.note: in places the edging word inside the word for study

parts.note: to con is to study or learn carefully
rims are edges, borders

explanation.surface: Learning that edges in a design are coloured a rich red.
explanation.walkthrough: CON, an old word for study or learn, holds RIMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a rich deep shade of red.

clue.text: Flightless bird about, so so cautious

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Flightless bird about, so so cautious' gives CA + SO + WARY = CASOWARY, one S short of CASSOWARY; 'so so' cannot supply SSO and the printed text likely misreads a word.
annotationWithheld.clue: Flightless bird about, so so cautious

clue.text: An obsession not easy to understand

explanation.surface: A fixation whose roots are hard to grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychological fixation is called this, and the adjective also means intricate or complicated.

clue.text: The garlic can make one sluggish

indicators.note: these letters can make a new word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Eating garlic leaves a person drowsy and slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' rearranges THE GARLIC; 'one' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic means lacking energy, slow and drowsy.

clue.text: Sausages from a Greek island

definitions.meaning: an island off Athens, site of a famous ancient naval battle

explanation.surface: Cured meats come from an island in the Aegean.
explanation.definitionFit: The cured sausage is spelt the same as the island near Piraeus where the Greeks defeated Persia in 480 BC.

clue.text: Sculpture about right height

indicators.note: about means around, so the sculpture surrounds the letter for right

parts.note: a statue is a sculpture

explanation.surface: A sculpture of roughly the correct height.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature means a person's natural height.

clue.text: Put up before court, editor

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Something was posted up ahead of a court case by a newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Erected means built or raised up.

clue.text: I had, disrupting contest — that's apparent

indicators.note: breaking into, so these letters go inside the word for contest

parts.note: an event is a sporting contest
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone admits they spoiled a competition, and it shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident means plain to see, obvious.

clue.text: Old writer ready to entertain new ideas

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A veteran author is receptive to fresh thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Being receptive or open-minded means willing to consider novel views.

clue.text: Run over

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a run not scored off the bat, such as a wide or bye

explanation.surface: Running past a limit.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, runs from byes, wides and no-balls are counted separately from the batter's own.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket run scored without the bat has this name, and the word also means surplus or additional.

clue.text: Help female with account, one italian brought in late

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside, so the letters go into the word for late

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman holding a bank account helps an Italian who arrived late.
explanation.definitionFit: To facilitate is to make easier, to assist a process.

clue.text: Ellen Terry's record

indicators.note: the 's stands for has, so the name has the letters within it

explanation.surface: An entry about the Victorian actress's achievements.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'has': ellEN TERry holds the word. Ellen Terry was a leading Victorian stage actress.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter details is to record them in a log or register.

clue.text: Cross with boy from Chinese city

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross
Ian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: An annoyed man with a lad from a Chinese city.
explanation.definitionFit: Xi'an is an ancient capital in China, home of the Terracotta Army.

clue.text: A gift, tart baked by one on Scottish island

indicators.note: baked means cooked, so the letters of tart are worked into a new shape

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde

explanation.surface: A present of a pastry cooked by someone living on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: An attribute is a natural quality or talent, which is also called a gift.

clue.text: I get excited cuddling hot little number

indicators.note: to cuddle is to hold close, so the rearranged letters wrap round
excited means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone gets thrilled embracing an attractive small person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges I GET into EIGT; 'cuddling' puts H inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight is a small whole number.

clue.text: Long period of time before end of depression

parts.note: a year is a twelve-month period

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A lengthy spell comes before the end of a slump.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn, to desire it strongly.

clue.text: Vehicle's condition in anticlockwise race

definitions.note: the 's is short for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: in places the word for condition inside the other word
going anticlockwise means running backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
state means condition

explanation.surface: A car's condition during a race run counter to the usual direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anticlockwise' reverses RACE into ECAR, and STATE goes in after the E. An estate car is the British term for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A car with an extended rear load area, called a station wagon in America.
